courses.title: Physical Geography
courses.description: [GE 5A] Basic principles of physical geography. Significance of earth-related distribution patterns with reference to their effect on human activities.

courses.title: Physical Geography Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] Basic principles of physical geography. Significance of earth-related distribution patterns with reference to their effect on human activities. Pre or Corequisite(s): GEO 1010 .

courses.title: Human Geography
courses.description: [GE 4A] Basic principles of cultural geography. Significance of people-related distribution patterns with reference to their effect on human activities. 3 hours lecture/discussion.

courses.title: Geographic Information Systems
courses.description: Presents geographic concepts in the framework of geographic information systems (GIS). Basic understanding of the theoretical basis of GIS and spatial data. Basic techniques for the computer processing of geographical systems analysis and modeling. Understanding of questions that GIS can answer. Corequisite(s): GEO 2400L .

courses.title: Geographic Information Systems Laboratory
courses.description: Presents geographic concepts in the framework of geographic information systems (GIS). Basic understanding of the theoretical basis of GIS and spatial data. Basic techniques for the computer processing of geographical systems analysis and modeling. Understanding of questions that GIS can answer. 3 hours laboratory. Corequisite(s): GEO 2400 .

courses.title: Introduction to Field Geography
courses.description: Introduction to the methods and techniques for collecting spatial and environmental data for physical geography and ecological studies. Corequisite(s): GEO 3090L .

courses.title: Introduction to Field Geography Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to the methods and techniques for collecting spatial and environmental data for physical geography and ecological studies. Corequisite(s): GEO 3090 .

courses.title: Remote Sensing of the Environment
courses.description: Principles and techniques of remote sensing using remotely sensed data to examine physical and cultural geographic scenes. Remote sensing applications in urban planning, agriculture, ecosystem management, atmosphere and earth sciences, and geographic information systems. Corequisite(s): GEO 4100L .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 2400 and GEO 2400L or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Remote Sensing of the Environment Laboratory
courses.description: Principles and techniques of remote sensing using remotely sensed data to examine physical and cultural geographic scenes. Remote sensing applications in urban planning, agriculture, ecosystem management, atmosphere and earth sciences, and geographic information systems. Corequisite(s): GEO 4100 .

courses.title: Senior Project/Capstone 1
courses.description: Exploration of research framework and research methods in geography. Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems.

courses.title: Climatology
courses.description: [GE 5D] Introduction to the fundamental concepts and theories in climatology. Methods of inquiry, including qualitative, quantitative, and computer based modeling and simulation methods. Explore climate variation through time and space and the reciprocal impact of climate and society. 3 hours lecture/problem-solving.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Global Environmental Systems
courses.description: Advanced concepts and theories in physical geography. Methods of inquiry, including qualitative, quantitative, and computer based modeling and simulation methods. The focus is on the geomorphological and hydrological processes on physical landform changes through time and space; and the interactions among physical environment processes and human activities. Corequisite(s): GEO 3050L .

courses.title: Global Environmental Systems Laboratory
courses.description: Advanced concepts and theories in physical geography. Methods of inquiry, including qualitative, quantitative, and computer based modeling and simulation methods. The focus is on the geomorphological and hydrological processes on physical landform changes through time and space; and the interactions among physical environment processes and human activities. Corequisite(s): GEO 3050 .

courses.title: Climate Change: Science and Action
courses.description: In depth investigation of the science of global warming and humankind’s impact on the Earth’s climate system. Corequisite(s): GEO 3070L .
courses.prerequisites: One course in GE Area B, GEO 1010 , GEO 1010L , or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Climate Change: Science and Action Laboratory
courses.description: In depth investigation of the science of global warming and humankind’s impact on the Earth’s climate system. Corequisite(s): GEO 3070 .
courses.prerequisites: One course in GE Area B, GEO 1010 , GEO 1010L , or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Cultural Geography
courses.description: An intermediate examination of the breadth, depth and methods of cultural geography through an examination of three themes: human-environment relationships; landscape; and place. The three themes are explored through the scholarship of selected distinguished cultural geographers. 3 hours lecture/discussion.

courses.title: Economic Geography
courses.description: Introduction to the substance and issues of economic geography. Topics addressed include the distribution and control of resources, the diversity of political/economic systems and the international exchange of labor and goods.

courses.title: Urban Geography
courses.description: Analysis and presentation on the problems in the origin and evolution of cities. Includes size, functions, distribution patterns, supporting and tributary areas, and roles within the whole political, social and economic structure of a region; includes suburbs and problems of metropolitan areas.

courses.title: Applied Cultural Geography
courses.description: Guidance and critiquing of student work in the analysis and evaluation of geographical characteristics of the natural environment and its human use. Includes field mapping, systematic and random sampling of spatial phenomena, and environmental impact reporting.

courses.title: GIS Programing
courses.description: Fundamental concepts in programing languages used in GIS. Focus on GIS script writing for frequently occurring tasks in customization and application development within a GIS system. Corequisite(s): GEO 3220L .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 2400 and GEO 2400L , or consent of instructor.

courses.title: GIS Programing Laboratory
courses.description: Fundamental concepts in programing languages used in GIS. Focus on GIS script writing for frequently occurring tasks in customization and application development within a GIS system. Corequisite(s): GEO 3220 .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 2400 and GEO 2400L , or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Geodemographics with Geographic Information Systems
courses.description: Application of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) techniques for the analysis of spatial and locational patterns of human population, population characteristics and population change. Housing, migration and commuting patterns. Market analysis and site location decision support. Neighborhood segregation and transitions. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement. Corequisite(s): GEO 4050LW .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 2400 , GEO 2400L , and junior or senior standing, or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Geospatial Data Analysis
courses.description: Quantitative analysis methods for research in the spatial sciences. Characteristics of geographic data (attributes of objects and fields in geographic space). Probability, hypothesis testing and confidence intervals. Summary, descriptive and exploratory statistics for geographic data. Regression modeling. Spatial autocorrelation and spatial regression methods. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement. Corequisite(s): GEO 4430LW .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 2400 , GEO 2400L , and junior or senior standing; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Advanced GIS
courses.description: Technical issues of geographic information systems. Topics include: data structures, database models, error estimation, and product generation. 3 hours lecture/problem-solving. Corequisite(s): GEO 4400L .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 2400 and GEO 2400L or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Advanced GIS Laboratory
courses.description: Technical issues of geographic information systems. Topics include: data structures, database models, error estimation, and product generation. 3 hours laboratory. Corequisite(s): GEO 4400 .

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Undergraduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
